qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Core Project Delivery segment (~75% of revenue) relies on competitive bidding for large-scale lump-sum and reimbursable EPC contracts against global engineering contractors (Bechtel, Fluor, Saipem). While the Technology, Products & Services (TPS) segment possesses proprietary process licenses (~15% EBITDA margin), the consolidated business lacks pricing power, operating at 5-7% Project Delivery margins exposed to project delays, geopolitical disruptions, and inflationary cost overruns.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3 (3a=None, 3b=N, REJECT). Technip Energies is a specialized energy infrastructure contractor with valuable LNG and decarbonization technologies. However, ~75% of revenue stems from lump-sum/reimbursable EPC contracts won via competitive bidding, resulting in low pricing power, thin segment margins (5-7%), and high vulnerability to cyclical energy capex.
qualitative.evidence: Project Delivery represents approximately 75% of consolidated revenues with recurring EBITDA margins of 5-7%. While net cash is positive due to client project advance billings, earnings are lumpy and project execution risks (e.g. Middle East logistical disruptions) cap pricing power across the energy cycle.
